title: Add latency-correlation-graph-generator and epoch synchronizer runner
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a reproducible way to surface cross-worker temporal correlations (e.g., multi-node p99 spike alignment, priming side-effects) that are lost when runs are treated as independent epochs. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) an epoch_synchronizer runner that coordinates epoch boundaries and priming windows across a distributed cohort of workers, and (2) a latency_correlation_graph generator that post-processes traces/latency buckets from synchronized epochs and emits a correlation graph and aligned heatmap artifacts suitable for downstream reporting and regression detection.

What this PR does: adds a new distributed runner (benchmark/runners/epoch_synchronizer.py) with an optional central coordinator mode and a peer-sync mode (gossip-based), implements a small clock-drift-tolerant barrier protocol to guarantee causal ordering of epoch markers, extends the runner harness to record an explicit epoch_id and wall-clock offsets per worker, and adds a post-processing tool (benchmark/reporting/latency_correlation_graph.py) that: ingests time-aligned latency streams, computes pairwise Spearman/Kendall correlations between worker-series, identifies likely causal lead/lag relationships via cross-correlation with significance testing, and emits: an annotated DOT graph (for quick visual inspection), an aligned epoch heatmap (Parquet + PNG), and a compact JSON summary suitable for automated regression pipelines.

Backwards compatibility: epoch_synchronizer is opt-in. Existing runners and reporting pipelines are unchanged unless the coordinator flag is enabled. The post-processor can consume legacy logs if a simple mapping layer is used (a short adapter script is included).

Checklist:
- [x] epoch synchronizer implementation with unit tests and integration harness emulation
- [x] post-processing tool with graph export and heatmap pipeline
- [x] CI workflow updates to run a small multi-node integration on PR builds
- [x] docs: new README and usage examples for running synchronized experiments
- [x] sample dataset and a short notebook for visualization (examples/latency-corr-demo.ipynb)

Performance/validation notes: Local integration runs (3-worker cohort, 1h synthetic workload) showed the synchronizer introduces 2-8ms median overhead to request scheduling (coordinator mode), but removes inter-epoch misalignment that previously caused false-positive correlations in p99 regressions. The correlation generator correctly recovered injected lead-lag patterns in synthetic tests (see bench/reports/controlled_injection_v0/*).

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the barrier protocol, property tests for the adapter mapping, and an integration job (ci/bench-integration.yml) that spins up a lightweight 3-node emulator in the PR runner. CI initially failed due to flaky timeouts in the emulator; fixed by increasing the default sync window and adding jitter to the peer gossip path. All checks are green on merge.

Docs and examples: Added a short guide under docs/bench/latency_correlation.md describing when to use synchronized runs, interpreting the correlation graph, and guidance on choosing coordinator vs peer-sync modes. The quickstart notebook demonstrates generating the DOT graph and exporting a PNG/Parquet pair for ingestion into the reporting pipeline.

Risks and future work: Current coordinator mode is single-point-of-coordination; future work will add an elected-leader mode with transparent failover. We also plan to add an ML-based anomaly scorer that uses the correlation graph as input to detect emergent cross-worker regressions automatically.

Related: ENG-8241 (evaluation of cross-node regression noise), ENG-8307 (benchmark suite reliability).
